claude_result_text:
I rebuilt the engine unit — but not the part the escalation notice pointed at, because that part was already done.

WHAT I FOUND BY LOOKING

I opened the contact sheet and views 1, 3, 5, 8, plus the planform (Virgin, underside), side (Air NZ) and front-quarter (Thai) references. The escalation told me to rebuild the nacelle as computed mesh geometry — but reading the source showed iter 14 had ALREADY done exactly that: the nacelle is a 18-point LatheGeometry body of revolution with computed vertex colours. Re-doing the lathe would have burned the iteration. So the lathe was never the bug.

The real defect is the PYLON, and it is measurable. The iter-14 blade was an 8.8 x 2.2 slab whose bottom edge ran from cx-1.3 to cx+1.5 — across essentially the whole 7.0-unit pod — and it was painted COWL, the same light tone as the nacelle it carried. So it plugged every bit of sky between the wing and the pod, and then colour-matched into it. Pylon and nacelle fused into one ~10x5 light mass in the side silhouette. That is literally every complaint on the board: "boxy nacelles" (v1), "blunt box nacelles ... no clear pylons" (v2), "simple cylinders floating near the wings rather than being properly pylon-mounted" (v5), "lack proper pylon mounting" (v9). Every one of those notes is about the slab, not the pod. In the references a 747 pod is slung forward and below, gripped only at its aft crown, with open sky visible above its whole forward half.

WHAT I CHANGED (engine block only)

1. Pylon rebuilt as a 5-point convex hand-built blade that grips only axial -1.75..+0.55 of the pod (26% of its length, all aft of the cowl bulge), rakes up-and-aft to a fairing tip at the wing leading-edge apex, and drops an aft heel below the wing like the strut fairing in the planform reference. The forward 34% of every nacelle (2.40 of 7.0, up from 1.55) now hangs in open sky.
2. Pylon painted a third tone (0x9fa8b2) that separates from both the light cowl it carries and the dark wing it hangs fro
